findings.summary: Builds on Ran's dual-manifold framework, in which one quantum state has two conjugate dynamical descriptions, on space-time M_xt and on the Fourier-conjugate momentum-energy manifold M_kE. A 'non-boundary' coupling (analytic continuation k -> k_r + i kappa) projects M_kE modes onto space-time as evanescent, non-propagating states with density rho(r) = rho0/(r + 1/kappa0)^2, cored and then falling as 1/r^2, which gives flat rotation curves. The paper identifies this projection with dark matter: it sources gravity and emits no far-field electromagnetic radiation. This is the round-1 lead g1 could not retrieve.
findings.difference: Shares C1's central idea: dark matter comes from the conjugate (momentum-energy) side of the description and gravitates in ours. The mechanism differs. The paper says dark matter is 'not a new particle species' but an evanescent projection produced by coupling two descriptions of one state. It has no matter species organized or localized in momentum, no spontaneously broken Born reciprocity or polarization order parameter, no x- and p-polarized sectors with strict P4, no gated self-interaction and no monopoles. Its halo profile follows from a chosen spectral weight A(kappa). Non-reviewed and removed from its host; INSPIRE lists no citations of the companion arXiv paper. Labelled partial (a close variant) under the brief's venue rule because it does state dark matter as the conjugate sector's appearance in space-time; a verifier may prefer related.

findings.citation: F. Bunchaft, S. Carneiro, "Weber-like interactions and energy conservation", Found. Phys. Lett. 10, 393 (1997), doi:10.1007/BF02764109, arXiv:gr-qc/9708047 (journal)
findings.summary: Studies velocity-dependent central forces of Weber type, k(r^/r)(1 - mu rdot^2 + gamma r rddot) as written in the abstract, as laws of gravitation: they conserve energy only if gamma = 2 mu, and a gravitational theory built on them cannot be conservative while also giving both Mercury's perihelion precession and light deflection. Reported as the representative of the Weber-type and relational-mechanics line the task names.
findings.difference: The Weber-type law is the classical precedent for a long-range attraction whose strength depends on the bodies' relative motion: for mu > 0 the factor (1 - mu rdot^2) is largest at zero relative radial velocity. But the velocity scale is c (mu of order 1/c^2, fixed by solar-system tests); only the radial component enters; it acts between all bodies; and it is not tied to dark matter or to clumping. C7's gate acts only among dark-matter particles, with width v* of order 100 km/s. The record's own O(v^2/c^2) analysis of spin-2 exchange (notes/velocity-gated-gravity.md §2) covers this regime. The paper's no-go weighs on Weber-like gravity in general, not on a chi-only gate.

not_found.statement: Outside arXiv and INSPIRE, no source other than Sheng Ran's removed ResearchHub preprint states that dark matter is the matter of momentum space, the conjugate or reciprocal sector, the dual half of phase space, or a mirror copy organized in velocity. Searched: OpenAlex titles, abstracts and full texts (until its budget ran out), DataCite (Zenodo, figshare, OSF, ResearchGate DOIs), the Zenodo API, Crossref, WebSearch (including viXra and Reciprocal System sites), Wayback, and the tangent-bundle, Carmeli, tachyon and Castro Perelman lines. The 2025-26 Zenodo/figshare flood of unified theories pairs dark matter with momentum-space, reciprocity or 'conjugate' wording without stating C1. Larson's Reciprocal System calls its 'cosmic sector' of 'inverse matter' the unobserved half of the universe but never identifies it with dark matter.

No source found, in any venue searched, in which dark matter clumps or condenses in velocity or momentum space through a collective instability, a Jeans analysis is run with position and velocity exchanged, or dark matter flocks by velocity. OpenAlex title/abstract phrase searches for 'clumping in velocity space', 'velocity space clumping', 'clumps in velocity space', 'condensation in velocity space' and 'Jeans instability' + 'momentum space' returned 0. Full-text hits are stellar moving groups, cluster substructure and cold-dark-matter fine-grained streams. 'Murmuration' hits are unrelated (elliptic-curve murmurations). DataCite and Zenodo hits are non-reviewed unified theories. The closest material remains what the known list holds (Sikivie-Yang, Berezhiani-Khoury, Zemp et al., Vogelsberger-White, Ghosh's Born-Kothari condensation).

No source found that states a long-range attraction among dark-matter particles acting only, or most strongly, between particles of similar velocity. The velocity-dependent gravity literature outside arXiv works at the velocity scale c or with absolute velocities, acts between all masses, and is offered as an alternative to dark matter or for perihelion precession. This covers Weber-like laws, Gerber-type fits (Gribkov), Arbab's generalized Newton law, Ghosh's inertial induction, Devasia's relative-velocity Weber model, Laletin's capture model and Hahn-Fine's measurement-induced attraction. None gates an attraction to small relative velocity at a scale like v* ~ 120 km/s, and none restricts it to dark matter. No Weber-type gravity paper applied to galaxy rotation curves was found (English and Portuguese searches). The closest remains Delbourgo-Lashmar 2008 (known: partial).

verdicts.reason: Metadata confirmed. Crossref: 'Dark Matter from Dual-Manifold Coupling', Sheng Ran, ResearchHub Technologies, Inc., type report, v1 2025-12-24, v2 2025-12-26. The PDF gives Dept. of Physics, Washington University in St. Louis and 'Dated: December 15, 2025'. The archived v1 record is status PREPRINT, with no peer reviews and not a version of record. Both pages return 404, and no copy exists on arXiv, INSPIRE, Crossref or the web, so the venue is non-reviewed. Companion confirmed: Phys. Rev. A 113, 042203 (2026), arXiv:2511.20907. Its arXiv title, 'Restoring a Missing Meta-Symmetry of Quantum Mechanics', is the PDF's ref. [8], and INSPIRE lists 0 citations of it. The finding's summary describes the paper accurately. DOWNGRADED to related, for two reasons. (1) C1 is an identity: dark matter is conjugate matter, the mirror-polarized counterpart of ordinary matter, the same kind of matter organized around momentum (as χ particles or momentum-localized monopoles). Ran states a different physical claim. Dark matter is 'not a new particle species' but 'an evanescent projection of a single quantum state across two dynamically conjugate manifolds', produced by coupling the two descriptions through analytic continuation (k -> k_r + i kappa). Its halo is a position-space |psi|^2 whose shape comes from a chosen spectral weight A(kappa) and a rescaling of r to galactic units. The paper never says dark matter is the counterpart of ordinary matter, or matter organized or localized in momentum. Its darkness comes from evanescence, and the paper says the framework 'does not impose any assumption about whether the underlying degrees of freedom carry electric charge'; C1's darkness comes from P4. What the paper shares with C1 is a theme: dark matter traced to the Fourier-conjugate momentum-energy half of a doubled quantum description, gravitating and dark. In the companion paper the same kind of projection yields dark energy instead. (2) The rule for non-reviewed works allows nothing above related unless the work states the conjecture itself, and this one does not. The label is consistent with round 1, which downgraded Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman, Leigh and Minic 2021 (2104.00802) to related because its dark matter was 'a class of metaparticle states, not a dual copy of ordinary matter'. The closest prior art for C1 remains the Minic lineage (known: anticipates and partial), which names the dual of each observed field as dark matter. Only v1 was read: v2 was deposited at 17:21 UTC on 2025-12-26, after the 05:10 UTC Wayback capture, and no archive holds it.

verify.notes: One finding verified (C1, Sheng Ran, ResearchHub). I checked the identifier, metadata, quotes, the 404 status and the Wayback capture independently. I refetched the PDF and the snapshot (both byte-identical to the sweep's copies), extracted the text with my own script, and checked the quotes two ways, with negative controls. Verdict: related (claimed partial). The paper shares C1's theme, dark matter traced to the momentum-energy half of a Fourier-doubled quantum description. But it says dark matter is 'not a new particle species' and makes it an evanescent coupling effect, not the mirror counterpart of ordinary matter. A non-reviewed work that does not state the conjecture itself cannot go above related. Side observations, not verdicts: (a) Ran's framework, one global state with two Fourier-conjugate dynamical descriptions, is closer to #11 App. A item 2 ('A coexisting conjugate universe — alive, transformed: one state, two descriptions') than to C1; App. A item 2 is not among C1-C7. (b) The paper's coupling phase winds by an integer in momentum space, Theta(k) ~ m arg(k - k0), 'providing topological protection to the resulting evanescent states'. This is a phase vortex of a coupling kernel with no magnetic charge. It is not C2, at most a neighbour by theme, and readers are unlikely to meet it now that the paper is removed. (c) The PDF's introduction says the companion reproduces a 'dark matter like background', but the companion's full text mentions only dark energy (lit.py text --grep dark: 5 matches, all dark energy). The phrase looks like a slip, and the companion's known label (C5 partial) is unaffected. (d) Ran has two more 2026 SSRN preprints in the same framework (doi:10.2139/ssrn.7447207, doi:10.2139/ssrn.7519471); their abstracts do not mention dark matter. (e) The archived record carries 'isResearchHubJournal': true, a submission through ResearchHub Journal, but its status is PREPRINT with no reviews. The ResearchHub API host did not resolve, so v2 could not be read. The output is in /home/paul/git/reinholdtsen/conjugate-matter/work/literature-check/round3/oa-c1-c6-c7.verify.json. findings.citation: S. Majid, B. J. Schroers, "q-Deformation and Semidualisation in 3d Quantum Gravity", J. Phys. A 42, 425402 (2009), arXiv:0806.2587 (journal)

not_found.statement: No work proposes magnetic monopoles, or magnetically charged topological solitons, localized in momentum space or abundant in a momentum-polarized, conjugate or reciprocal sector, as matter or as dark matter. Searched beyond arXiv and INSPIRE: OpenAlex title/abstract (0 hits for "momentum space" AND monopole(s) AND dark matter/sector; 3 for phase space + magnetic charge + dark matter; all 253 records of "magnetic monopoles" AND "dark matter" read by title and filtered by abstract); DataCite (Zenodo, Figshare, OSF: 118 and 45 hits, all Berry-curvature physics or unrelated); Crossref posted content (Preprints.org, SSRN, OSF, Qeios, Research Square: 4 queries); WebSearch in English, Russian and Chinese and on viXra. Every monopole-dark-matter proposal found puts the monopoles in position space; every 'monopole in momentum space' is a Berry-curvature or bundle object (collisions: Majid-Schroers, Onoda-Tatara-Nagaosa).

No work explains the absence of observed monopoles by their being localized in momentum, or in a conjugate, reciprocal or dual space, rather than in position. The explanations found outside the known list use another time flow or universe (Henderson 2025, non-reviewed), a superposition of +-g with zero mean charge (Barut 1972), confinement inside every particle (Kursunoglu 1974), binding into monopole dimers (H. Liu 2026, Zenodo/Figshare, non-reviewed), or gravity forbidding monopoles (S. Maes 2020, OSF, non-reviewed). The one title that might state C3's argument, Khademi and Nasiri's 2009 talk 'Why magnetic monopoles are not seen?', could not be read (unverified leads).

No work places a magnetically charged counterpart of every electrically charged particle in a dual, conjugate, reciprocal or momentum-space sector. Full magnetic counterpart families appear only in ordinary space (Sullivan-Fryberger 2015, Fryberger 2018, Polchinski's completeness, Krasnoholovets 2019); a dark sector of magnetic charges under its own photon appears without any position-momentum structure (García-Moreno-Vento 2026, after Vento 2025); and works joining Born reciprocity, Fourier or T-duality to electric-magnetic duality do so formally, inside one theory (Jafarizadeh-Rezaei-Aghdam 1999, De Haro-Cinti 2025, Kriger 2026, the last excluding monopoles). No work combines S-duality and Born's rho to put the magnetic half of electromagnetism in the p-polarization (the shared-photon form).

verdicts.reason: Confirmed partial, narrowly (medium confidence). This is the same label as Vento 2507.06697, whose model this paper restates. METADATA: INSPIRE (recid 3210647), the arXiv API and the arXiv abs page agree: J. García-Moreno, V. Vento, 'Electron and monopole properties in a dark matter model', hep-ph, v1 of 1 Oct 2026, v2 of 8 Oct 2026, 11 pages. There is no journal-ref, DOI or Crossref record, so it is an arXiv preprint only. Its Funding line names Springer Nature open-access funding, which suggests a journal submission that is not yet on record. WHAT IT STATES (read in full, secs. 1-9): Sec. 2 restates Vento's two-photon QED. A_mu 'is the ordinary photon that couples only to particles with electric charge', and C_mu is 'the extraordinary photon that couples only to particles with magnetic charge'. 'The new photon and the monopoles form the dark matter sector.' 'For simplicity we will consider ordinary matter to be made just of electrons and dark matter just of monopoles.' The Schwinger condition eg/sqrt(1-eps^2) = n (eq. 13) ties the dark magnetic coupling to e. 'In order to generate a portal we assume a kinetic mixing between the photons.' This has the sector structure of C4's separate-photon form: our matter is electric under our photon, and the dark matter is magnetic under the dark sector's own photon, with a coupling inverse to ours through a quantization condition. WHY NOT MORE: (1) There is no mirror. The paper has one monopole species, and the electroweak extension enlarges only the visible side ('The aim was to enlarge the Standard Model into the dark sector, consisting of a photon and monopoles'). Nothing says that each charged particle has a magnetic analog. (2) There is no position-momentum polarization, no Born reciprocity and no S-rho identification. The dark sector is an ordinary hidden sector, and 'mirror', 'dual', 'momentum space', 'phase space' and 'reciproc' do not occur in the text. (3) The coupling relation is the Schwinger condition, imposed together with the mixing, not reciprocity acting as S. Both make the magnetic coupling inverse to e. (4) The portal is kinetic mixing, which strict P4 excludes. (5) The paper's new content is the electroweak extension (secs. 5-8). It mixes the dark photon with hypercharge and makes it massive ('To this theory we incorporate Higgs fields to endow masses to the heavy bosons and the dark photon.'), which moves it further from the separate-photon form, whose p-sector photon is massless. (6) 'Dark matter' is only a label. The paper has no relic abundance, no Parker bound and no cosmology. It computes laboratory observables only: an electron g-2 bound on eps, a Biot-Savart test, and e+e- to monopole pairs, plotted at a monopole mass of 1 TeV. WHY NOT LESS: I weighed a downgrade to related. The generic hidden-U(1) monopole dark matter on the known list is labeled related (Terning-Verhaaren 2018, which is this paper's ref. [12]). This paper goes beyond it in two ways: it makes the split between the visible and dark sectors the split between electric and magnetic charge, and it ties the two couplings by a quantization condition. Those two points are what is specific to the separate-photon form, so partial stands, as a close variant of one form and not as the conjecture. USE: All of its C4 content comes from 2507.06697 (its ref. [17]), which frames the model more explicitly ('We depart from Cabibbo and Ferrari in that we will ascribe the monopoles to dark matter.'). Cite the two papers together as one model, not as a second, independent anticipation. If the consolidation counts arXiv-only preprints as non-reviewed, this work does not count, because it does not state the conjecture itself.

findings.citation: D. Mukherjee, H. K. Jassal, K. Lochan, "Bouncing and collapsing universes dual to late-time cosmological models", Eur. Phys. J. C 84 (2024) 318, doi:10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-12673-1, arXiv:2207.02835 (journal)
findings.summary: Uses the Einstein-frame/Jordan-frame (conformal) correspondence of scalar-tensor gravity to give the dark-energy-driven late universe a dual description: a ΛCDM Einstein frame always maps to a bouncing Brans-Dicke Jordan frame, and quintessence plus matter to a Jordan-frame turnaround, a bounce or a collapse. The abstract concludes that the effect of dark energy can equivalently be seen as collapse of space in a conformally connected universe. Two passages beyond the abstract bear on C5's route. Sec. 6 runs the map the other way: a de Sitter Jordan frame (Brans-Dicke parameter -4/3), which mimics the dark-energy-dominated era, has as its Einstein-frame dual a stiff fluid (w = 1, zero potential, a purely kinetic scalar) that contracts toward a crunch. That is the pairing of #11 §10's 'dual stiff ↦ Λ' with the stiff side contracting, realized in another duality. Sec. 5.2's thawing example uses the hilltop potential Λ⁴(1 + cos(φ/f)), the functional form of #11's τ potential V₀[1 + cos(τ/f)], and arranges the Jordan-frame collapse at the current era, which bears on the open question of how the route relates to τ's potential.
findings.difference: The dual description is a conformal (Weyl) rescaling of the same spacetime in a scalar-tensor theory, fixed by the Brans-Dicke field, not the momentum-space description of Born reciprocity, and no relation like a·ã = 1 holds (in sec. 6 the Einstein-frame scale factor goes as (1 - const·t̃)^(1/3) while the Jordan one grows exponentially, eq. 47). Dark energy (Λ, quintessence or the Brans-Dicke field) is put in by hand in one frame; the collapse in the other is a re-description ('equivalently', 'alternatively'), not its source, so C5's 'drives' is absent, though #11 App. A item 8 reads its own duality as synchronized, not causal. The turnaround point is tunable through the Brans-Dicke parameter, and for ΛCDM the dual is a bounce, not a collapse. The stiff/de Sitter pairing of sec. 6 is one exact solution (ω_BD = -4/3, U = 0), not a dictionary w_eff = -w̃. Not anticipation: the conjecture's partner is the momentum-space (conjugate) description, and here it is a conformal frame. The g4 verifier reported this paper (g4-collapse-acceleration/verify.json, new_findings; it read the abstract and secs. 3 and 8); it is not in round3/known.json. Sec. 6 and the sec. 5.2 hilltop example are not in that entry.

findings.summary: The first paper of the expansion-collapse duality line. It reconstructs the f(R) Jordan-frame duals of quintessence-driven Einstein-frame cosmologies and finds, for a class of viable quintessence models, that the Jordan-frame universe grows to a maximum size and then collapses while the physical (Einstein-frame) universe keeps expanding; it derives the condition for this duality for time-varying equations of state with matter present.
findings.difference: Conformal frames of f(R) gravity, not Born reciprocity or momentum space; the dark energy is assumed (quintessence) and the dual collapse is a mapping at the level of the field equations, not a source; no inverse scale factor, no dictionary; this paper does not yet say that the collapse is the effect of dark energy (the 2024 paper does). Also in the g4 verifier's new_findings; not in known.json.

quotes.text: We show that for certain class of viable quintessence models, the Jordan frame universe grows to a maximum finite size, after which it begins to collapse back.
Thus, there is a possibility that in the late time limit where the Einstein frame universe continues to expand, the Jordan frame universe collapses.
This mapping between an expanding geometry and a collapsing geometry at the field equation level may have interesting potential implications on the growth of perturbations therein at late times.

findings.summary: Kadyshevsky lineage (de Sitter momentum space of radius M, the 'fundamental mass'). Rodionov's school recasts Kadyshevsky's geometric model as a non-Hermitian Dirac theory with a gamma5 mass term and a maximal mass M, and conjectures that the 'exotic' fermions present in both versions are constituents of dark matter. It continues the known Kadyshevsky, Mateev, Rodionov and Sorin 2007 (0708.4205, C1 related), where the exotic fermion field comes from a second factorization of the de Sitter momentum-space wave operator and its quanta are conjectured to be dark matter. The titles of the 26 and 24 INSPIRE citers of 0708.4205 and hep-ph/0512332, and an abstract filter on the citers of the older Kadyshevsky papers, show no other dark-matter proposal.
findings.difference: The exotic fermions are a new fermion species whose polarization and mass properties are fixed by the curvature of momentum space; they are not ordinary matter in the mirror polarization, are not organized or localized in momentum, and carry no velocity gate or momentum clumping. not_found.statement: No paper in the lineages swept (Kadyshevsky; Wheeler-Hazboun; Caianiello and pseudo-complex GR; Yukawa-Takabayasi bilocal fields; Born, Fuchs, Green, Cheng, Rodriguez; Weber-Assis; Petit-Janus and Bondi negative mass; Moffat; Tomilchik; Castro; Pavšič; Bars 2T physics; Majid; Snyder-Yang; tangent/cotangent-bundle and Finsler gravity; Carmeli) states that dark matter is ordinary matter in the momentum (mirror) polarization, organized around momentum and gravitating like ours. Their dark-matter proposals are exotic fermions from a curved momentum space (Kadyshevsky, Rodionov), geometric dust (Hazboun-Wheeler, known), negative-mass twin matter (Petit), a gauge-invisible doubled fermion copy (Pavšič), fibre-symmetry charges (Herrmann), the dilaton or right-handed neutrinos (Bars), an effect of accelerating frames (Castro, known), standard candidates inside pseudo-complex GR (Hadjimichef, Volkmer), or velocity-dependent geometry replacing dark matter (Finsler: Chang and Li; Carmeli).

No lineage paper proposes magnetically charged solitons localized in momentum space, or an abundant population of them as dark matter. Monopole language appears only as an effective geometric force produced by a curved momentum space (Kupriyanov, Kurkov, Sharapov 2024, collision). Citers of the Kadyshevsky anchors filtered for 'monopole' or 'magnetic charge' return nothing else; Tomilchik's monopole papers (1975-1996), by their titles, concern P-invariance and dyon spectra, not momentum space.

No lineage paper explains the null result of monopole searches by localization in momentum space. Unverified lead only: Kadyshevsky, Mateev and Mir-Kasimov 1975, 'Solution of the charge quantization problem' (bibliographic record only).

No lineage paper pairs each electrically charged position-polarized particle with a magnetically charged momentum-polarized analog, or ties S-duality to Born's rotation. Born's school wrote a 'Reciprocity theory of electrodynamics' (Born, Cheng, Green, Nature 164, 281 (1949)); only its first paragraph was reachable, and it concerns divergences.

No lineage paper states that the gravitational collapse or contraction of a momentum-space (conjugate) description of our universe drives our accelerating expansion, or that stiff (kinetic-dominated) content of such a description acts on ours as a cosmological constant. Nearest analogs: a second matter population's clustering or repulsion (Manfredi, Rouet, Miller 2026; Petit and d'Agostini 2014), collapse of our own structures (Räsänen 2006, outside the assigned lineages), and dark-energy terms from momentum- or velocity-space geometry (Hazboun-Wheeler, Moffat, pseudo-complex GR, Ibadov-Murodov, kinetic-gas Finsler gravity, tangent-bundle cosmology, Carmeli).

No lineage paper proposes that matter clumps in momentum or velocity space through its own collective attraction. The lineages treat momentum space as curved geometry (Born, Kadyshevsky, Moffat, Wheeler), a velocity fibre (Finsler, tangent-bundle, Caianiello), or a source of velocity-dependent gravity (kinetic gas), never as a space in which matter gathers into clumps.

No lineage paper proposes a long-range attraction among dark-matter particles that acts only at small relative velocity. The velocity-dependent gravity of the Weber-Assis lineage weakens the attraction with relative radial speed on the scale of c and acts on all bodies (Assis, Relational Mechanics, Apeiron 2014, eq. 25.15, read in the author's PDF); the record already cites this lineage (notes/velocity-gated-gravity.md §3, Tisserand 1872). Ghosh's velocity-dependent inertial induction is applied, by its titles, to redshifts, solar-system anomalies and flat rotation curves; its abstracts were not reachable (unverified leads).
